Config is:
```

SizeMinBytes=10G
SizeMaxBytes=120G
GrowFileSystem=yes
```

review_comments: Hmm, why "x" and "r"? Maybe call this something more descriptive.
I do not know, I just followed the names used in the above block.
This is a noop, because `xsz < share => xsz < UINT64_MAX` (`=>` in the sense of implication) …
Yeah, so I dropped `xsz != UINT64_MAX`, as it is redundant.
Hmm, is the whole commit supposed to change behaviour?
similar, return 0 here if `a->after` is NULL?

if this is now a helper of its own, maybe also add a code path dealing with the first free area, i.e. where `a->after` is NULL. In that case you can just return `free_area_available()` after all the offset is zero...
Does this have any effect on the logic? After looking at the commit, I don't see anything…

Previously, this did not return UINT64_MAX, but returned a huge value. This fixes a theoretical issue, `xsz < share` may be true for sooooo huge disk. In realistic situations, this commit does not change anything.
